# Rock de Vocht

> I design systems that understand, prove them with running code, and lead the engineers who build them.

Software architect · technical leader · hands-on developer · technical AI consultant.
Based in New Zealand. Website: https://peter.nz

## Biography
Rock de Vocht is a software architect and hands-on technical leader with a Master of Science in
Computer Science from the University of Auckland and a 30-year record of designing systems that other
engineers build on. He has co-founded two companies, defined the technical roadmaps and reference
architectures behind two enterprise semantic search platforms, and led teams of up to ten engineers
through the full SDLC.

He designs at the whole-system level — data model, service decomposition, integration surface,
security boundary, deployment topology — and then writes production code alongside the team. His
expertise spans full-stack engineering, infrastructure, networking, security and cloud, with deep
specialisation in big-data retrieval, NLP and complex API integration.

As a technical AI consultant he translates between executives and engineers: pre-sales and solution
architecture at Datacom, CTO-level technical advisory at Booktrack, and architecture reviews and
whitepapers for clients today. That advisory work now centres on AI: where language models are
load-bearing, how their reliability is measured, and what governance the result has to stand up to.

## How he works
- Designs in the open and validates by building. Decisions are written down, walked through with the
  team, and proven with a running slice before the wider build commits to them.
- Stays hands-on in the codebase so the architecture stays honest, and optimises for the engineers
  who have to live in it.
- Democratic, social and highly collaborative as a lead. Takes responsibility for the team's
  mistakes, mentors junior staff closely, shares knowledge freely, and consistently prioritises
  results over ego.
- Methodologies: RM-ODP, MVC, micro-services, SaaS, Agile and Waterfall.

## At a glance
- 30+ years engineering
- Teams of up to 10 engineers led
- 2 companies co-founded
- 20+ successful projects delivered

## Career history
- **Senior Developer (Contract), Nylon** — Jun 2026 to present.
  Leading the ISO 42001 implementation (the AI management standard) and standing up the measurement
  system for LLM reliability underneath it, including test data creation. Reviewed the document
  processing architecture and delivered optimisations to ingestion and learning-from-documents.
  Investigated language model performance across the product's real workloads and authored a
  whitepaper covering methodology, benchmarks and recommendations. Built a reusable LLM evaluation
  harness in Node.js so model quality, latency and cost stay measurable as models and prompts change.
  Stack: Node.js, TypeScript, Python, Qdrant, AWS, PDF extraction, LLM evaluation and benchmarking.

- **Chief Scientific Officer & Co-Founder, SimSage UK Ltd (Cambridge, UK)** — Jan 2020 to Apr 2026.
  Owned the architecture and delivery of a graph-based enterprise semantic search engine, from data
  model and service decomposition through to deployment topology. Directed a 250k+ line codebase with
  30+ enterprise API connectors (SharePoint, OneDrive, Google Drive) and production AI workflows
  integrating Gemini, OpenAI and Copilot. All jobs and requests routed through Kafka to independently
  scalable services. Designed the security protocols and RBAC model governing sensitive enterprise
  data across every connector and tenant. Led and mentored a team of three.
  Stack: C#, Kotlin (JVM), Java, C, Python, React + TypeScript, SQL, CQL, Kafka, Kubernetes,
  Terraform, Ansible, Docker, Ubuntu Server, GitLab CI/CD.

- **Developer (Contract), MBIE / NZ Immigration (Wellington)** — May 2018 to Dec 2019.
  C# .NET and SQL development on Azure within Linux environments. Designed and ran the unstructured
  data integration and NLP processing of 170 million text records for signal analysis, using Python
  for data manipulation and machine learning for data quality analysis.

- **NLP Specialist, Booktrack.com (Auckland)** — Mar 2016 to May 2018.
  Advised the CTO on development strategy and machine learning / NLP direction. Researched and
  developed neural networks for emotional text analysis and contextual understanding within the
  company's core IP. Core development in C#, SQL, Java and Python across Google Cloud and Azure, on
  Kubernetes and Docker.

- **Developer / DevOps (Contract), Verifone (Wellington)** — Jan 2015 to Mar 2016.
  Managed CI/CD and DevOps operations, analysing and resolving critical system bugs, and taking
  ownership of complex technical issues escalated to level-three support.

- **Chief Scientist & Co-Founder, SYL Search (Wellington)** — May 2008 to Jan 2015.
  Defined the technical roadmap and designed a semantic search engine adopted by several NZ Government
  departments (MOT, NZTA, MPI). Led a development team of five through the full SDLC and IP creation.
  Designed and managed complex integrations with external APIs, SharePoint, CRM and social platforms.
  Stack: Java, C#, SQL, Cassandra.

- **Senior Architect, Microsoft Team, Datacom (Wellington)** — Jan 2004 to May 2008.
  Solution architecture for Datacom's enterprise customers as a member of the internal Datacom
  Architecture Solution Group. Pre-sales technical assistance and technical writing, competing in
  several large projects with teams of up to ten engineers. Team lead, mentor, and runner of internal
  education sessions.
  Stack: .NET Framework, ASP.NET, C#, SQL Server, SharePoint, Windows Server.

### Earlier career

## Projects
Built and run in a home lab — one server, no cloud account. Index and architecture records:
https://home.peter.nz/

- **pi and piview** — a Prolog interpreter in C++ written to be read as much as used: a hand-written
  recursive-descent parser, a flat node stack, an indexed name/arity database, and no third-party
  dependencies. Runs at a prompt or over TCP, with every client sharing one database. piview adds a
  live web view and a Kotlin MCP server exposing seven typed tools, so a clause typed at the prompt,
  one asserted by an agent, and the listing in the browser are the same database changing under each
  other in real time. ~7,000 lines of C++, 0 dependencies.
  Source: https://github.com/rock3125/pi

- **Seshat** — a chat application over a private folder of text files, and an MCP server. Answers come
  back with the paragraph they were drawn from attached, so the citation opens the source text rather
  than a summary. Hybrid retrieval: BM25 keyword matching and dense embeddings, fused server-side by
  reciprocal rank fusion. One Kotlin jar is both the MCP server and the chat gateway, so a browser and
  an agent reach the same tools from one definition. Kotlin, React.
  Source: https://github.com/rock3125/seshat

- **pdf-redaction** — a Java PDF redaction library that actually redacts. Common tools draw a black
  rectangle and ship a PDF whose content stream still contains every word underneath; this one
  intercepts the text operators, strips the characters while holding the visual layout together, and
  re-encodes any raster image overlapping a redaction zone with the pixels blacked out.
  Rotation-aware, metadata stripped on save, no online service involved. Java 17+, PDFBox 3.x,
  Apache 2 licence.
  Source: https://github.com/rock3125/pdf-redaction
  Maven Central: https://central.sonatype.com/artifact/nz.peter.pdfredaction/pdf-redaction

- **G-Force X** — a momentum-based cave flyer on HTML5 canvas. Thrust adds to velocity as in
  Asteroids, and the cavern has two media: air pulls the ship down, water floats it up and thickens
  the drag. Terrain is generated by cellular automata then flood-filled so every pocket connects.
  Play: https://home.peter.nz/gforce/
  Source: https://github.com/rock3125/gforcex-js

- **Super Asteroids** — vector arcade in three.js. The ship is pinned to the centre of the view and
  the universe is translated around it, so rocks spawn into a ring outside the viewport and are
  collected further out, keeping the field infinite while the live entity count stays flat.
  Collisions filtered through a layer matrix; vector line under a bloom pass; audio synthesised in
  the browser.
  Play: https://home.peter.nz/super-asteroids/
  Source: https://github.com/rock3125/super-asteroids

- **Space Invaders** — the 1978 cabinet rebuilt in a canvas element with no framework and no build
  step. Eleven columns by five rows, one shot on screen at a time, bunkers that erode block by block,
  and a step interval scaled to the number still alive (0.9s with the formation full, 0.05s with one
  left).
  Play: https://home.peter.nz/spaceinvaders/
  Source: https://github.com/rock3125/spaceinvaders
